strategies.name: overnight_range_break_retest_continuation
strategies.entry_summary: Mark the overnight/pre-market high and low, then wait during the New York session for price to break one side of that range with confirmation: strength for an upside break or weakness for a downside break. After the break, wait for a pullback/retest of that broken level and enter in the direction of
strategies.exit_summary: Place the stop on the opposite side of the breakout level: below the prior overnight high for longs, above the prior overnight low for shorts. Manage by taking continuation in the breakout direction, optionally trimming profits and moving the stop to breakeven, or exiting quickly if price closes

variants.variant_label: Long continuation after break above overnight high
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: Break above overnight high with strength, then bullish retest candle/price action such as bullish hammer, bullish engulf
variants.target_note: Open-ended continuation; examples mention about 1.5R to 2.6R and also trimming then moving stop to breakeven
variants.transcript_quote: if we break above the overnight highs, we want to see it break with strength above, but then we want to see it pull back and test this area as support

variants.variant_label: Short continuation after break below overnight low
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: Break below overnight low with weakness, then bearish retest candle/price action such as bearish hammer, gravestone doji
variants.transcript_quote: if price were to break below this level again, we're going to look for it to break with weakness. We then want to see price come back up, test this

result.enumeration_note: One strategy taught: the same overnight-range break-and-retest continuation skeleton is presented for both long-above-high and short-below-low directions; these are compatible directional variants with mirrored entry/stop logic, not separate opposing strategies in the same context.
